These sort of silly party games are typically not my thing. I played through the tutorial. Free weekend so why not, right? My younger son loves these so we'll probably give it a go later, and I'll update my review.

[h3]AI[/h3]
The AI voice in the trailer video was more jarring than the AI assets in the game, but it's clearly still there and about as detracting as you might expect it to be. I won't neg the game just for AI use, but if you hate AI you'll most likely hate it here. I do wish Steam had better tools to note AI generated content and maybe filtering for those who don't want it. Negative reviews from haters don't help the non-haters, and positive reviews from gen AI supporters are not much use to people who refuse to buy AI content.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
The game itself played okay. The targeting could be a little cleaner, the rats look a little glassy-eyed and hollow, the French accent was... certainly a choice. It didn't crash in my relatively short playtime. I can already see there appears to be a good bit of complexity in recipes and equipment and ingredient availability. This could become annoyingly complex as the game progresses, but it was fine in the tutorial. Grilling mushrooms to create a dish called "Fried Mushrooms" felt more lazy than humorous. There isn't much "immersion" here but I understand it's made to be a silly fun game to play with friends, complete with Twitch integration.

[h3]Audio[/h3]
The sounds are pretty generic, the music was... I wasn't pay

Alright so I'll freely admit, I really thought this was going to be streamer slop. Some crap that was designed not for fun but for streamers/youtubers to play in groups yelling at each other and getting into all that "whacky" shenanigans. The opening trailer on the steam page gave me those vibes and nearly put me off from wishlisting it entirely. 
 
So imagine my surprise to discover that this is actually a very well crafted and designed game. Its like PlateUp but less focus on ball busting time management and more on the finer details of running a restaurant. Keeping stock of all your inventory, choosing where patrons sit to keep conflicting races separate (♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ based), prepping ingredients to expedite cooking processes. In PlateUp, the prep phase was just reorganizing things and making sure your automation was set up correctly. In this, you gotta precook some stuff like the damn Chefs Special Soup which takes 5 whole ass ingredients and nearly a full minute to cook. And of course, 4 of those 5 ingredients need to be chopped so you're not just chucking a whole ass potato in there and the last ingredient is a well done steak so guess what else needs to be done during prep. But you can't just cook all the dishes and let them sit, they will expire and turn to globs of goo you have to clean.

My hubby got us this game because we love playing Overcooked and other games that include running our own business, especially restaurant oriented ones. I have to say we LOVE IT!  
We had play so many of different games that just didn't hit the spot like Restaurats did, we didn't expected a lot at first, but our jaws dropped as soon as we started the tutorial.  
There is so many options to dress up your rat, so many different recipes that ngl are kinda hard at first with prepping, cutting, baking and grilling. There is just so many different things to do and I believe this is one of the best games for couples that came out in recent months.  
So if you have a partner that you love to play with, consider getting it! The price is also laughable, the AAA companies would easily charge over 30/40$ for it with dumb microtransactions or battle passes for outfits. Restaurats give you all of that at one price and it makes sure you play enough to get your moneys worth back. 10/10.

So, I randomly stumbled upon this game on YouTube right before the big Steam sales, when my friends and I were looking for something to play. The moment I saw it, I looked at the boys and said: "BUY IT. NOW." The price is an absolute steal for a co-op game that can easily suck you in for hours.

BUT DON'T LET THE CUTE LOOKS FOOL YOU. THIS IS A DAMN DRUG. We are grown-ass men who just wanted to grab a beer after a long work shift, kick back, and relax. Instead, what are we actually doing? Sweating bullets, screaming orders at each other with shaking voices, running around the kitchen like absolute maniacs, chain-smoking through the stress, and turning on each other over a ruined dish. No mistakes are forgiven here. None.

The game captures the actual work vibe way too realistically. Even though I know there’s no boss standing over my shoulder and nobody is rushing me, I’m genuinely terrified to take a break if the tomatoes aren't chopped yet. And when that Vampiress shows up and we fail her order? I feel real-life shame.

Realism: 10/10
Total friends left: -2

Devs, please expand the game universe so that after a brutal shift in the kitchen, I can go visit my personal rat therapist. 10/10 would ruin friendships again.

I've been playing this game for the past few days and we all love it. It's the most satisfying cooking game we've played yet. We like the game loop and preparing for the day. They have already prepared ingredients you can buy if you don't feel like chopping etc. 

In friendslop mode, it is a little frustrating when you encounter a new VIP and the game is instantly over because you handled them wrong, but because of the RPG character improvement aspect, it's not like you're starting entirely from scratch. 

The only two things that take away a little from the experience for me, are the box/shelf system and the character movement. For me, the realistic having boxes and unpinning to move them around is not a fun mechanic. It would be nicer to spend less time by having ingredients just box up when put into a shelf.  Full boxes could just replace empty ones or empties could disappear when the last item is taken. Movement-wise, I get motion sick in some games and this is one of them. Usually games have several options that I can tinker with to help avoid it. In this game, I mostly stay in the kitchen and that helps. I like cooking, but every time I have to run down a tunnel or turn a corner, I don't feel great. It's not so bad I haven't been able to play. Oops, one more, it'd be great to have the delivery guy sound less icky. That detracts rather than adds anything to the game.

All in all though, it's one of the best impulse buys we've played in a long time. I'm always looking for

If you ever want to test if your friendship can survive a nuclear apocalypse, play this game.
I started playing thinking I’d be a Michelin-star chef. Two minutes later, the kitchen was on fire,

Honestly, Restaurats is such a fun game. It’s genuinely challenging in the best way. My friend and I play as a duo, and it actually forces real conversations about how we want the restaurant to run each day—which is awesome and surprisingly intense.

The game throws tons of interesting, dynamic events at you that keep you on your toes and stressed… but in that good, gamer way 😄

While restaurant customization could use a bit more love (and it’s already on the roadmap), the character customization is fantastic—and completely free, which is a huge win.

Overall, great game. Thanks to the devs! Your hard work is really paying off 👏🍽️

So. 
This might look like a cute lil rat game, like a cute lil lets-cook-and-greet-customers-game but hear me out. 
Dont be fooled by the cute little rat noses, funny outfits or smooth designs. 

This is war. 

You need to get faster.
You need to get more efficient. 
You need to learn to optimize your processes. 
You need to look better.
You need to gamble harder.
You need to be nicer to the guests.
You need to know what they want; 
YOU NEED TO BE IT ALL.

Good fun, especially with a few friends. The novelty does last, and the gameplay loop is solid. Nice to see the devs continuing to take feedback and make updates that improve balancing and QoL. As other reviews have mentioned it is very prep heavy, you probably spend 70% of your time prepping food, 20% ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around knocking your friends out with baguettes and messing with cosmetics, and 10% actually serving customers. You could probably get more than 20 hrs out of it if you do some of the arcade modes- we did 14 hours or so in the campaign and felt like we pretty much saw what was on offer. If I have any feedback, its maybe to tweak the progression in the campaign a bit and have some extra variety. The events and VIP interactions are fun, but they didn't happen very often. When most of the game is prep, it would be nice for the shift time to have more variety from day to day since that's where a lot of the chaos can ensue.

Great purchase, this game is a ton of fun with challenge. I played on challenge and the pace of play is a perfect high tense relaxing tempo. I love the moment you start to feel comfortable with the game then the game hits you with an event that creates at least seven skeleton customers to overwhelm you. 
I currently have 12 hours on this game and I had 26.7 on the Playtest. 

The creators of this game had fast turnaround times for documented complaints in the Playtest, and even some fun changes they kept to LAUNCH yourself or a friend. I'd recommend this game to anyone who wants a family friendly relaxing game.

Learning curve is fairly easy, games difficulty levels makes it playable for brand new to experienced players.

For Restaurats Team:  Anti-bet hammer saved me from my friends, Thank you! I only need one restaurant. I love the details on the delivery troll. The voice line addition was great. Would love more customizable kitchen items, I.E. four stocks of storage, I had it in Playtest, but now i am just waiting for it to be an option. Keep up the great work
